case_name: State of Punjab v Sarwan Singh
respondent:
Sarwan Singh
Supreme Court of India

19 November 1996
Cr.A. No. 1977 of 1996
The Order of the Court was as follows:
Leave granted.
1.  We have heard learned counsel on both sides.This appeal by special leave relates to nature of the offence committed by him.
2.  The admitted position is that on October 25, 1985 at about 6 a.m. in village Kahlon within the jurisdiction of the Police Station Nawahshahr, one Santokh Singh and his party and the respondents ad their party had a dispute on land. They indulged in quarrel as a result of which Santokh Singh died. The courts below recorded a finding that the occurrence had taken place at 6.00 p.m. in which both the parties sustained injuries.
3.  The deceased Santokh Singh received as many as 8 injuries five of which were on the head. As per the evidence of PW-2 the autopsy doctor, he died of the multiple injuries on the head. The injuries were inflicted with a gandasa.
4. According to the ordinary course of nature. Therefore
facts: The admitted position is that on October 25, 1985 at about 6 a.m. in village Kahlon within the jurisdiction of the Police Station Nawahshahr, one Santokh Singh and his party and the respondents ad their party had a dispute on land.
They indulged in quarrel as a result of which Santokh Singh died.
The courts below recorded a finding that the occurrence had taken place at 6.00 p.m. in which both the parties sustained injuries.
The deceased Santokh Singh received as many as 8 injuries five of which were on the head.
As per the evidence of PW-2 the autopsy doctor, he died of the multiple injuries on the head.
According to the ordinary course of nature.
It is clearly a case under Clause thirdly of Section 300, IPC and of murder punishable under Section 302, IPC unless the case is brought in any one of the exceptions engrafted is S. 300 IPC.
issues: Culpable homicide is not murder if it is committed without premeditation in sudden fight in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel and without the offender's having taken undue advantage or acted in a cruel or unusual manner.
respondent_arguments: The parties had to fight over dispute of land.
It is not the case of the accused that he had acted in self-defense of him or others and in exercise thereof, he inflicted the injuries.
court_reasoning: The respondent cannot escape the offence.
Obviously, therefore, S. 149 IPC was not rightly applied and this Court refused leave as against the acquittal of others.
It is implicit that he had taken undue advantage and acted in a cruel or unusual manner in inflicting four heavy blows on the head resulting in death of Santokh Singh.
holding: The conviction by the courts below u/ss. 304 IPC, Part I, therefore, is set aside.
The offence is one of murder punishable u/s. 302 IPC and accordingly, the respondent is convicted of the offence and is sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life u/s. 302 IPC.
